spec.title: PROP-067 — The terminal display language: blocks, a gutter, a fold, one palette

status.comment: Drafted 2026-11-01 on the owner's request, from three screenshots of Claude Code's conversation view; built the same day in crates/vibe-cli/src/output/language (the one drawing module), with golden captures under crates/vibe-cli/tests/golden/display.

p.purpose: The owner is not satisfied with how vibe looks in a terminal. The surfaces that exist — the step panel, the plan, the prompt theme, the listings — were each drawn on their own, and together they read as several tools. The reference the owner named is Claude Code's conversation view: a vertical stream of blocks that never touch, a one-column gutter of status glyphs, finished work collapsed into one short summary line, one restrained palette, and metadata that is always dimmer than the text it annotates. This document derives from that reference a set of rules for an ordinary line-oriented terminal, with no mouse and no full-screen application, and binds every human-readable output of the CLI to them: `vibe install`, `vibe install -g`, `update`, `app plan`, `self update`, `remap list`, the wizard, every listing, every refusal.

p.principle: A terminal screen is a page with a gutter. Everything the CLI writes is a **block**: one line in the gutter says what the block is and in what state, the rest is indented under it, and a blank line separates it from the next block. What is finished collapses to its one gutter line; what is running shows its last few lines; what the reader wants in full is one key or one flag away, and its path is always printed. Colour names a role, never decorates: five roles and nothing else. Nothing is ever glued to its neighbour, nothing is boxed, and the same vocabulary draws a plan, a running step, a question and an error.

p.block: A block is a gutter line followed by zero or more body lines. The gutter line is `<glyph> <headline>` — the glyph in column 0, one space, the headline from column 2. Body lines start at column 2 as well, so every line of a block shares one left edge, and a wrapped headline continues at column 2. The headline is a sentence fragment that names the thing and its state in that order (`build Build vim`, `installed org.vibevm.apps/vim@9.1.0`), with metadata after it joined by ` · ` (`#meta`). Blocks are separated by exactly one blank line; the first block of a command has no blank line above it and the last has none below. No two gutter lines are adjacent unless the group is a **list** (`#list`).

p.gutter: Column 0 belongs to the glyph alone, and the glyph set is closed: `●` a block that is running or a message being written now; `✓` a block that finished well; `✗` a block that failed; `○` a block that was skipped or is waiting its turn; `✻` the trailer of a command (`#trailer`); `?` a question (`#question`); `!` a warning that is not a block of its own; `│` the fold of a running block (`#fold`) and `└` the child of a block (`#children`). The ASCII set for a terminal that reports no vocabulary is `*`, `+`, `x`, `-`, `*`, `?`, `!`, `|`, `` ` ``. The spinner of a running block replaces its `●` in place while it spins and is restored when the block is redrawn. No other glyph, no emoji, no box-drawing corner, no bullet appears in column 0 anywhere in the CLI; a tree inside a block (`#children`) lives at column 2 and deeper.

p.fold: A running block whose child writes output shows a **fold**: its last five lines, each prefixed `│ ` at column 2, in the `dim` role, bounded to the viewport width, redrawn in place as new lines arrive. Under the fold one dim hint line names the expansion: `(l to show the live log)` on an attended terminal, nothing when unattended. The fold is the terminal's answer to "click to expand": the key `l` switches the block to its live stream, `--log live|tail|quiet` and `--log-tail N` decide it ahead of time, and the collapsed line of the finished block (`#collapse`) prints the path of the full log. The fold's lines are never coloured by their content; a child's own escape sequences are stripped. A block whose child writes nothing shows no fold and no hint.

p.collapse: When a block finishes, its fold and hint are erased and the block is redrawn as its one gutter line with the completion glyph and the metadata of what happened: `✓ build Build vim · 2m 10s · 412 lines`. The count of lines says there is a log and how large it is; the trailer (`#trailer`) says where. A failed block keeps its last thirty lines under `│ ` in the `text` role (not dim: they are now the evidence) and ends with `✗ build Build vim · 2m 10s · exit 2 · log <path>`. A skipped block is `○ docs Copy the documentation · skipped: feature docs off` in the `dim` role. Collapsed blocks of one command form a list (`#list`), so the finished screen is the plan with its answers written in. The failed block is drawn gutter line first — `✗ build Build vim · 2m 10s · exit 2 · log <path>`, the path shortened in its middle — with its thirty kept lines under it, so it keeps the shape of every other block.

p.fact: Consecutive items of one kind — the steps of a plan, the rows of a listing, the finished blocks of a run, the answers of a wizard — form a list: adjacent gutter lines without blank lines between them, and the whole list is one block separated from its neighbours by the usual blank line. Inside a list the columns are aligned on plain text across the whole list: the glyph, the name, the kind in parentheses, the title, then the metadata; a column that no row uses is not drawn. A list that would exceed the viewport height is not paged; it scrolls, because the summary line that matters is the trailer and the reader scrolls back for detail.

p.children: A block that contains other blocks — a step that installed a requirement first, a command that runs several steps, a listing with per-row providers — draws them as a tree starting at column 2: `└ ` before each child's headline, the child's own body under it at column 4, the grandchildren at column 6 with their own `└ `. The branch glyph is always `└`, never `├`, because a row is written when its block ends and nothing then knows whether a sibling follows (PROP-060 `#DISPLAY`); the parent's collapse closes the group. Depth is limited to three visible levels; deeper structure is summarised by a count in the metadata (`· 4 more`). A finished child keeps its completion glyph in column 0 and its `└ ` at column 2 (`✓ └ fetch Fetch the toolchain · 3s`), so the state of every row is read in the one gutter.

p.heading: A section inside a command — the plan, the answers, the listing's second group — opens with a **rule**: `── <label> ` followed by `─` to the viewport width, in the `dim` role, the label in the `text` role. A rule is a block of its own (blank line above and below). The label is lower case and names the section (`plan for org.vibevm.apps/vim@9.1.0`, `rows by source`, `answers`). A right-aligned label on a rule (`──── Architect`) is reserved for context that is not the section's own — the invoking tool under `--invoked-by`, the home under `-g` — and appears at most once per command, on its first rule. No other kind of header exists: no capitalised words, no underlines, no boxes.

p.meta: Metadata is everything that annotates a headline rather than being it: elapsed time, sizes, counts, exit codes, a path, a state word. It follows the headline after ` · ` (space, middle dot, space), item by item, in the `dim` role, except that a count or a size that changes what the reader does is in the `text` role and bold (`412 lines`, `12.4 MB of 12.4 MB`, `3 unreachable`). A state word (`detected`, `installed`, `hidden`, `offered`) is set in brackets at the end of the row, `dim`. Time is written as the shortest exact form: `0s`, `3s`, `2m 10s`, `1h 4m`. A path is written in full once, in the trailer, and shortened in the middle elsewhere (`~/.vibe/cache/app-runs/…/2026-11-01T10-51/`); an identifier (a package key, a step id, a launcher key) is never shortened.

p.palette: Five colour roles and no sixth: `text` (the terminal's default foreground), `dim` (the terminal's bright-black / faint attribute: every rule, every metadata item, every fold line, every hint, every skipped block), `accent` (one hue — the terminal's blue or its 256-colour lavender where the capability is reported; every identifier inline in prose: package keys, step ids, flags, paths, file names, the highlighted row of a selector), `ok` (green: `✓`, the answered value of a question, a successful trailer), `alert` (red: `✗`, a refusal's headline, a `deny` row) and `warn` (yellow: `!` and the headline it marks, `unencrypted`, `broad`, `update available`). Bold is used for counts in metadata and for the value a question was answered with, nowhere else. A background colour is used only for the selected row of a selector and for nothing else. Every colour sits on an attribute the terminal maps itself, so a light theme and a dark theme both read; no RGB is written by the CLI. `NO_COLOR`, a redirected stream and `--plain` print the same text with no attribute at all, and the layout stands without colour because the glyph and the indentation already carry it. The accent is the terminal's blue; no capability probe picks a 256-colour hue.

p.inline: In human-readable output an identifier is set in the `accent` role and never in backticks; backticks belong to the JSON, the specs and the logs. A sentence names at most one identifier per clause. A command the reader can type is on its own line, indented at column 2 under the sentence that introduces it, in the `accent` role (`fix` lines of a refusal, the `(l to show the live log)` hint, the trailer's `see`). The sentences the libraries write into an error keep their backticks for now: the same sentence is the `error` field of the `--json` envelope, and a refusal draws it as its headline and its `why`.

p.question: A question is a block: `? <prompt>` in the gutter, its choices as a list under it at column 2 with the selected row highlighted, the key legend as one dim hint line under the list, a blank line before and after. When answered, the block collapses to `✓ <prompt> <value>` with the value in the `ok` role and bold — exactly the shape of a finished step, because a question answered is work done. The wizard's answers therefore accumulate as a list at the top of the screen, above the rule that opens the plan. The shared prompt theme of PROP-065 `#display` is the implementation of this paragraph; its column rules (name, id, description, detected) are the `#list` rules applied to choices. `dialoguer` draws no footer under a list, so the key legend is printed once per process, dim, above the first list question rather than under it. A yes-or-no question whose body is the thing being decided — a remap offer, the download of the documentation shell — prints that body under its `?` gutter line before the prompt, and only the prompt collapses: the body stays above the `✓` line as the record of what was answered, and the collapsed line may say what was decided (`✓ remap offer accepted org.corp/intranet`) rather than `yes`.

p.refusal: A refusal is a block with `✗` and a headline that says what was refused, in the `alert` role: `✗ consent_required 1 remap package offer needs an answer`. Its body is label columns at column 2 — `why` (one sentence), `fix` (one or two commands on their own lines), `see` (the spec address) — labels in `dim`, values in `text`, commands in `accent`. The code is the first word of the headline so that a reader who grepped a log finds it in the gutter line. A warning that does not stop the command is `! <sentence>` in the `warn` role, one line, inside the block it concerns or alone between blocks; it never gets a body. The error envelope under `--json` is unchanged by this paragraph (PROP-065 `#error-codes`). The block is read from the error itself: the application's stable code (or a `snake_case:` lead word), the sentence before its `(violates …; fix: …)` tail as the headline, the spec address as `see`, the backticked `vibe …` commands of the fix — or the fix sentence when it names none — as `fix`, and the cause the chain adds as `why`, whose own fix comes first. Quiet mode keeps its one line: `✗ <code> <message>`.

p.trailer: Every command that did work ends with one trailer block: `✻ <what happened> · <how long> · <where the record is>` — `✻ installed org.vibevm.apps/vim@9.1.0 · 3 steps · 2m 14s · log ~/.vibe/cache/app-runs/vim/2026-11-01T10-51/`. It is the one line a reader keeps: the glyph `✻` is used for nothing else, the headline is in the `ok` role on success and the `alert` role on failure (`✻ failed at build · 2m 10s · log …`), and the path is written in full. A command that only listed or explained has no trailer; its last list is its answer. A command that was parked or needs a decision ends with a trailer whose headline says so (`✻ parked at step agent-review · resume with`), followed by the command on its own accent line. A parked trailer is drawn in the `warn` role: it is neither a success nor a failure. The count is the number of finished blocks the run drew; the record is the run directory of the latest step log.

p.width: Lines are bounded to the viewport. A headline wraps at a word and continues at column 2; a fold line, a metadata item and a rule are cut at the viewport edge with `…` at the end; a path is shortened in its middle before it is cut; an identifier is never cut — the metadata after it is dropped first. Columns of a list are measured on plain text over the whole list before it is drawn, so a late long row does not shift the earlier ones; a list that does not fit the width drops its rightmost column first (the metadata), then the title, never the name. A redirected stream has no viewport: its lines are neither wrapped nor cut, so a log keeps every sentence on the line a reader greps for, and its rules run to eighty columns. Metadata that does not fit a list leaves the row first, onto a dim line of its own under the title column, so nothing the row says is lost; then the title is dropped, never the name.

p.plain: A redirected stream, a dumb terminal or `--plain` receives the same blocks in the same order, with no cursor movement, no spinner, no fold and no in-place redraw: a block is written once, when it ends, as its collapsed line; a running block that is silent for longer than the waiting interval of PROP-060 `#DISPLAY` writes one dim `● <headline> · still running · 30s` line. The blank line between blocks, the gutter glyphs (in the ASCII set when the terminal reports no vocabulary) and the indentation are kept, so a log file reads as the screen did. `--json` is a different surface and this document does not touch it; `--progress-format json` events are unchanged. Under `--plain` a step's child output stays in its log unless a `--log` mode is named, so the stream holds the blocks alone; a redirected stream keeps the live child stream PROP-065 `#display` defaults it to.

p.coverage: The rules bind every human-readable output of the CLI, drawn by one module that owns the glyphs, the roles, the rule, the block, the list and the trailer: the progress renderer of PROP-060 (the panel is a stream of blocks with folds), the plan and the wizard of PROP-065, the catalog listings of PROP-059, the remap views of PROP-066, `vibe self`, `vibe list`, `vibe check`, the `init` wizard, every refusal. No command composes its own glyph, colour or separator; a command that needs a shape this document does not name amends this document first. The test that guards it is the one PROP-065 `#display` already has for the prompt theme, widened: no `console::style`, no `dialoguer` theme, no hand-written glyph, no box glyph spelled as an escape and no `vibe: warning:`-style prefix outside the one module. Covered by name: project `vibe install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `cache import`, `cache clean`, `vibe init`, `vibe self install|update|reinstall|use|rollback|import|remove|gc` and the foreground `vibe app start` end with a trailer (the last one on stderr, because stdout belongs to the program that ran); `vibe self ls|current` is a measured list with `[active]` and `[running]` state words and the source execution under a rule of its own; `vibe check` draws its findings as blocks under a rule and closes with a summary, because it only reports; every question — `init`, the install confirmation, `reinstall`, `mcp`, `self remove|gc|source`, `skill`, `clean`, `cache clean`, `doc shell`, `update`, `uninstall`, the remap consent and uninstall questions, the app wizard — is asked through the one set of prompt helpers of the module and collapses to `✓ <prompt> <value>`; a remark that is neither a step nor a warning is a dim hint line, and consecutive hints touch. `vibe tree`'s plain view keeps its tree of `├`/`└` (its rows are all known before the first is written), drawn with branches the module owns and spelled in ASCII where the terminal reports no vocabulary. Two deliberate exemptions: the full-screen interfaces `vibe tree` and `vibe prefs` draw their own screens, outside a line-oriented terminal's blocks, and are exempt from the guard; and the PROP-060 progress rows of `vibe self` (`[done] Activating installed version [715ms]` and their kin) stay the progress renderer's, the trailer following them as the last block. Under `--quiet` a project command keeps the one summary line its quiet contract already prints (`vibe install: …`, `vibe update: …`, `vibe uninstall: …`, `vibe init: …`, `vibe cache …: …`), because scripts read those lines; the trailer is the human mode's. Test modules name the glyphs they assert.

p.example:
`vibe install -g org.vibevm.apps/vim` on an attended terminal, mid-run, under these rules (the first list is the wizard's answers, the second the plan, then the running block with its fold): ``` ✓ Platform Windows (windows) [detected] ✓ Installer msys2 (windows/x86_64) result owned ✓ Features core, docs
── plan for org.vibevm.apps/vim@9.1.0 ────────────────────── installed by vibevm-app
1. fetch (sources) Download the sources 2. build (recipe) Build vim needs command:gcc └ requires org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@15.2.1 (build, hidden) [installed] 3. docs (copy) Copy the documentation
✓ fetch Download the sources · 12.4 MB · 3s
● build Build vim · 14s │ compiling object 58 of 60 │ compiling object 59 of 60 │ linking vim.exe (l to show the live log) ``` and the same screen when the command has ended: ``` ✓ fetch Download the sources · 12.4 MB · 3s ✓ build Build vim · 2m 10s · 412 lines ✓ docs Copy the documentation · 0s
✻ installed org.vibevm.apps/vim@9.1.0 · 3 steps · 2m 14s · log ~/.vibe/cache/app-runs/org.vibevm.apps__vim/2026-11-01T10-51-02/ ``` A refusal under the same rules: ``` ✗ consent_required 1 remap package offer needs an answer, and this run has nobody to ask why org.corp/intranet is offered and neither accepted nor rejected fix vibe remap accept org.corp/intranet vibe remap reject org.corp/intranet see spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-066#consent ```

p.decisions: **No mouse, so a key, a flag and a path.** Claude Code expands a collapsed block on a click; a terminal line has no click. The three substitutes are already in the tree (`l`, `--log`, the printed path) and this document only makes them the one rule. **No full-screen renderer.** An alternate screen would allow panels and a status bar; it would also hide the scrollback that is the whole value of a line-oriented tool, and the owner's shell (`vibevm-app`) is where a status bar belongs. Rejected. **Five roles, not a theme.** A configurable palette was considered and rejected: the terminal already has one, and five attribute-mapped roles read on every theme without the CLI knowing which. **`└` only.** `├` would need the renderer to know the last sibling before it is drawn; PROP-060 settled this and the plan now follows the renderer rather than the other way round. **One module.** The failure this document exists to end is each command drawing its own look; the rule that no command composes a glyph or a colour is what prevents its return.

p.acceptance: Golden captures under `script` of `vibe install -g` (attended, with a fold; unattended; failing at a step), `vibe app plan`, `vibe remap list`, `vibe app list -g` (the CLI has no `vibe list -g`), one refusal, `vibe self ls` over a store of two instances, `vibe check` with one finding, the unattended `vibe init`, the `consent_required` refusal and a project `vibe uninstall`, compared as plain text after stripping attributes; a unit test that the glyph and role tables are the only source of glyphs and attributes in `vibe-cli`; the existing prompt-theme guard widened to every styled call; the plain-mode capture of the attended run reads block for block as the attended one.

p.changelog: 2026-11-01 — drafted from the owner's screenshots of Claude Code's conversation view: block, gutter, fold, collapse, list, children, heading, meta, palette, inline, question, refusal, trailer, width, plain, coverage; example screens for `install -g` and a refusal. 2026-11-01 — built: `output::language` owns the glyphs, roles, rule, block, list, meta, trailer and refusal; the panel, the plan, the wizard, refusals, warnings and the app and remap listings draw through it. Amended where building found the draft silent or impossible: the failed block's order (`#collapse`), a finished child's glyph (`#children`), a redirected stream's width and metadata that does not fit (`#width`), the accent hue (`#palette`), library error prose (`#inline`), the legend's place (`#question`), how a refusal is read from an error (`#refusal`), the parked trailer's role and the count (`#trailer`), `--plain` and the child stream (`#plain`), the full-screen interfaces (`#coverage`), `vibe app list -g` (`#acceptance`). 2026-11-01 — coverage finished: trailers on project `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `cache import|clean`, `init`, the `vibe self` verbs and the foreground `app start`; `vibe self ls|current` as a measured list; `vibe check` findings as blocks; every question through the module's prompt helpers, the remap consent as a `#question` block (PROP-066 `#consent`); `vibe tree`'s plain branches from the module; the remaining `warning:` and `note:` prefixes as `!` diagnostics and dim hints; the guard widened to box-glyph escapes and the `vibe:` prefix; a decided body stays above its collapsed answer (`#question`). Named in `#coverage`: the two exemptions (the full-screen interfaces, the PROP-060 progress rows of `vibe self`), the trailer of a foreground program on stderr, and quiet mode's one summary line kept for project commands.
